title: European Commission hit by cyberattack affecting staff payroll and leave systems
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Izvestia, relaying a Politico report, says the European Commission has faced a major attack for more than 10 days. Most staff were paid as usual, but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave. A Commission spokesperson, Thomas Rainier, said individual systems were attacked, those affected were notified and some applications were suspended. Whether employee data was taken is still being checked.
plain: The European Commission says some of its internal systems were attacked and some applications were switched off. Most staff were paid as usual, but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave.
exec: An attack on an EU institution's HR systems puts staff personal data at risk.
action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
impact: Some applications temporarily suspended; possible exposure of employee data not yet established.

validation.note: Izvestia article relaying Politico; Politico original and a Commission statement not read. Nacionale also headlines the attack (redirect link not read).

review.note: Compared with Izvestia (relaying Politico): duration, spokesperson, suspended apps and data check match; fixed overstated payroll wording (most paid as usual; some could not file time sheets or arrange leave). Politico original not read; stays single_source.
